projects.title: Project Lift, Elevator Proposal Automation
projects.meta: 2025 · Developed in-house at IEEI · Vertical Transport · Mitsubishi Electric
projects.summary: Excel/VBA proposal generation that connects pricing and technical specifications in one repeatable workflow.
projects.body: Context Problem: Proposal generation for Mitsubishi home elevators required manually updating identical specifications across three separate documents, error-prone and time-consuming. Client/Use: Developed in-house at International Elevator & Equipment, Inc. (IEEI, subsidiary of Mitsubishi Electric) during employment tenure. Role Responsibilities: Sole developer, designed the automation logic, built the VBA interface, and tested across all Mitsubishi specification variants. Tools: Microsoft Excel, VBA. Process Implemented a "portal" technique in VBA: a single master input cell combination drives synchronized updates across the proposal sheet, technical specification sheet, and pricing sheet simultaneously. Key Challenge: Preventing circular update loops, resolved by controlling event trigger sequences through Application.EnableEvents management. Results Eliminated redundant manual entry. Reduced proposal turnaround time significantly. Zero cross-document discrepancies after implementation.

projects.title: Thesis, Nonlinear Seismic Analysis: Three Resilience Techniques
projects.summary: A five-story school study comparing seismic-response strategies through time-history analysis.
projects.body: Context Problem: Existing 5-story public school structure in Agoo, La Union lacked adequate seismic resilience documentation for Seismic Zone IV conditions. Client/Use: Academic thesis research, Technological Institute of the Philippines. Role Responsibilities: Designed and analyzed three independent seismic resilience systems, base isolation, buckling-restrained braces (BRBs), and steel-plate shear walls, and compared their performance using nonlinear time history analysis. Tools: ETABS, SAP2000, NSCP 2015, ASCE 7. Process Modeled the existing structure and applied each retrofit system independently. Ran nonlinear time history analysis using ground motion records scaled to site hazard levels. Evaluated inter-story drift, base shear, and floor acceleration responses across all three systems. Key Challenge: Calibrating nonlinear material properties for each system, required iterative pushover runs before committing to time history analysis. Results All three systems demonstrated measurable improvement over the unretrofitted baseline. Comparative findings documented per NSCP 2015 performance objectives.
contributions: Time history and nonlinear pushover analyses for strength, stiffness, and resilience
Comparative evaluation of seismic techniques with design recommendations

projects.title: Project BOQ, Estimation Workbook Audit & Repair
projects.meta: 2026 · Personal / Reference Build · Structural BOQ Estimation
projects.summary: Schema-based BOQ workbooks and estimation workflows for repeatable civil project planning.
projects.body: Context Problem: A comprehensive BOQ estimation workbook (earthworks through roof framing, rebar detailing, and steel schedules) had accumulated formula errors and inconsistent detailing logic across dozens of interconnected sheets, undermining confidence in the output quantities. Client/Use: Personal reference build used to standardize how I estimate structural quantities. Role Responsibilities: Full audit and repair, sole developer. Traced formula errors sheet by sheet, corrected detailing conventions against code, and rebuilt weak sheets as parametric calculators. Tools: Microsoft Excel, structural code references (NSCP 2015, ACI 318-14). Process Audited every sheet (earthworks, footing, column, beam, slab, wall footing, masonry, finishings, roof, schedules, BOQ, steel materials, lighting & fixtures) and fixed over 180 formula errors. Corrected rebar detailing logic to follow bar-diameter-proportional conventions instead of flat assumptions. Rebuilt the roof sheet as a parametric truss calculator and repaired subtotal gaps across the BOQ summary. Added a change log sheet to track every revision going forward. Results A workbook that now produces consistent, code-aligned quantities across every structural component, with a documented history of what changed and why. Current work also includes a Python BOQ builder: a canonical 24-sheet workbook schema, 17 divisions, an interactive build menu and schema validation.
contributions: Canonical workbook schema, interactive builds and validation

projects.meta: 2025–2026 · Personal Project · MPLE Board Exam Reviewer
projects.summary: An updated gamified study and review tool, evolved from the earlier review engine.
projects.body: Context Problem: Preparing for the MPLE board exam meant grinding through the same static reviewer PDFs and question sets repeatedly, with no structured way to track coverage or force real repetition over time. Client/Use: Personal study tool, built for my own MPLE and Materials Engineering review. Role Responsibilities: Sole developer. Designed the data pipeline, the cycle/draw logic, and the front-end review interface. Tools: Python for question-bank processing, HTML/CSS/JS for the local review engine. Process Built a local, file-based review engine that ingests structured question banks (currently 615 MPLE and Materials Engineering items) and serves them through a "cycle" system: draw a question, answer it, track completion percentage per cycle, and start a new cycle once the pool is exhausted. Filtering by module and category is supported so review sessions can be scoped narrowly instead of always drawing from everything. Local, file-based question bank with draw/answer/next-question flow, no server required

sections.title: Project overview
sections.text: Independent engineering software development combining civil engineering, numerical methods and programming. My role: Project Creator, Engineering Logic Developer & Validation Lead.

sections.title: Problem and objectives
sections.text: Engineering calculations can become fragmented across manual solutions, isolated tools and reports. The objective is an organized workflow in which inputs, assumptions, results and calculation procedures can be reviewed together.

sections.title: My contribution
sections.text: I developed engineering approaches, mathematical formulations, pseudocode and algorithm flowcharts. I used AI-assisted coding for implementation, debugging and refinement, while independently checking whether the calculations behaved as intended.

sections.title: Technology and architecture
sections.text: A Flask/Python application connects numerical analysis routines with browser-based JavaScript workspaces and diagrams. NumPy supports numerical work; Matplotlib and ReportLab support reporting. Deployment configuration includes Docker and Waitress.

sections.title: Implemented in the inspected source
sections.text: Beam and truss analysis workflows, an experimental frame workspace, selected reinforced-concrete and steel calculation helpers, load-related tools, projects, reports and a Code Navigator. Feature depth and validation differ by module; navigation entries do not establish completion.

sections.title: Deployed application
sections.text: The public beta dashboard and beam workspace were accessed on 21 October 2026. A simply supported 6 m beam with a 10 kN downward midspan load returned 5 kN reactions, 15 kN·m maximum moment and 2.8125 mm deflection for E = 200 GPa and I = 8 × 10⁻⁵ m⁴. This is a single checked example, not platform-wide validation.

sections.title: Testing and verification
sections.text: The inspected validation evidence records 20 independent closed-form prismatic-beam comparisons passing within their stated tolerances. I also use independent manual solutions and benchmark comparisons to investigate discrepancies in equations, assumptions and decimal precision. Recorded repository tests and this live example have different scopes.

sections.title: Engineering methodology
sections.text: Identify governing equations, assumptions and boundary conditions; derive the calculation sequence; implement it; solve representative problems independently; compare benchmarks; then correct and retest discrepancies. Distributed-load development seeks a generalized formulation rather than unrelated hardcoded cases.

sections.title: Known limitations
sections.text: Public beta under active development and verification. Experimental and unsupported cases remain, including gaps recorded for support settlement and equation-load workflows. Inspected local release-candidate evidence does not prove that identical code is deployed. This is not fully validated or certified structural design software.

sections.title: Development roadmap
sections.text: Expand systematic tests and validate individual modules, improve calculation traceability and refine engineering reports before treating outputs as dependable design tools.

sections.title: Lessons from the work
sections.text: A functioning interface is insufficient evidence of engineering correctness. Explicit assumptions, independent solutions and a reviewable calculation trail are central to a credible engineering tool.

sections.title: Project overview
sections.text: A personal knowledge and project-continuity system that connects a local web workspace with SQLite records, Markdown notes and Obsidian-compatible links.

sections.title: One project, evolving scope
sections.text: Second Brain is the foundation of this project, not a separate current product. It expanded into Life OS and now includes project review, documentation and agent-assisted workflows. Earlier knowledge-system and review-register work belongs to this development history. Individual integrations retain their implementation and verification limits.

sections.title: Problem and objectives
sections.text: Project context can become scattered across folders, notes and unfinished work. The objective is to retain discoverable project context and observed changes so future work can resume from evidence rather than memory alone.

sections.title: Technology and architecture
sections.text: Flask serves the interface and APIs, SQLite stores local application records, and Markdown files provide portable documentation. Browser JavaScript handles project and documentation workflows. Local project registration and the documentation observer are separate from optional cloud AI authoring.

sections.title: Implemented in the inspected source
sections.text: Project registration and workspace cataloguing; documentation drafts and reviewed filing workflows; a local observer that scans registered source folders, produces linked project summaries and dated observed-change records, and preserves source files and curated notes. Private and generated folders have exclusion rules.

sections.title: Automatic documentation workflow
sections.text: While running, the observer checks registered projects every 60 seconds and waits for changes to settle across scans. It records observed source evidence; it does not invent the reason for a change, infer milestones or claim that tests ran. Markdown links support navigation inside an Obsidian vault.

sections.title: Testing and verification
sections.text: Ten tests from the actual automatic-documentation module passed again in an isolated workspace. A synthetic sample project was also processed with the actual observer. Broader historical application regression records were inspected but were not rerun against the private production workspace.

sections.title: Screenshot evidence
sections.text: The actual Life OS documentation template is shown with isolated sample API data. The production databases and private vault were not connected. This captures the source interface, not a claim that all application services were exercised. No private knowledge graph is shown.

sections.title: Privacy and AI boundary
sections.text: The deterministic observer runs locally without automatic AI calls. Optional Lane B authoring uses cloud AI when enabled and sends selected context; local-first does not mean every feature is offline. Review and provider permissions remain necessary for that optional workflow.

sections.title: Known limitations and deployed status
sections.text: A local personal system, with no public application deployment verified. Observed change records are not a complete version-control history. Automated decision tracking, all past save states and verified off-device backups should not be assumed. Integrations have their own configuration and availability limits.

sections.title: Development roadmap
sections.text: Improve continuity and review workflows, strengthen regression coverage and clarify sync, recovery and integration status. Expand knowledge connections using explicit recorded evidence without exposing private notes.

sections.title: Lessons from the work
sections.text: Useful continuity depends on separating observed facts, human decisions and AI-authored explanations. Portable Markdown and explicit review make the documentation easier to inspect and carry forward.

sections.title: Project overview
sections.text: A civil engineering and quantity-surveying automation project connecting reviewed drawing inputs, engineering quantity calculations and an Excel bill of quantities.

sections.title: Problem and objectives
sections.text: Manual transfer between drawings, schedules and spreadsheets creates repeated entry and makes quantity origins difficult to trace. The objective is to reduce that transfer while retaining explicit engineering review of assumptions and mappings.

sections.title: Technology and architecture
sections.text: Python and ezdxf read CAD entities through explicit mappings. Workbook adapters connect quantities to an Excel estimation system, with browser interfaces for BOQ review. The workflow keeps drawing interpretation, calculation, spreadsheet recalculation and release checks as separate responsibilities.

sections.title: Implemented in the inspected source
sections.text: Mapped DXF entity counts, straight-line lengths and closed straight-polyline areas; explicit unit conversion; reviewed target-cell mappings; extraction evidence and drawing hashes. Additional workflows cover footing/member inputs, concrete and reinforcement calculations, stock-length optimization and workbook summaries. Those paths retain assumptions and input requirements.

sections.title: Tested in an isolated sample
sections.text: The actual extraction module processed a new synthetic millimetre-unit DXF: a 6 m beam line, a 6 m² slab outline and four column markers. The outputs matched 6, 6 and 4. An open polyline requested as an area was rejected. This narrow test does not validate a complete building estimate.

sections.title: Recorded verification and release state
sections.text: Repository status records workbook reconciliation and alternate-engine checks. Native Excel validation remains pending in that record. The project handoff also identifies newer estimation interface work; the installed workbook baseline should not be mistaken for a finished end-to-end release.

sections.title: Screenshot evidence
sections.text: The screenshot uses the actual read-only BOQ viewer with a newly created synthetic workbook. Rates and totals are demonstration values only. No client drawing, estimate or source workbook was copied into the portfolio.

sections.title: Known limitations
sections.text: Extraction requires reviewed mappings, supported geometry and declared units. It does not infer a complete BOQ from arbitrary CAD. Curved geometry and incomplete schedules require review. Revised inputs, rates and native Excel recalculation/release validation remain prerequisites for a final estimate. File preflight alone is not takeoff validation.

sections.title: Deployed status
sections.text: No public estimation deployment was verified. The portfolio presents local development evidence rather than a production estimating service.

sections.title: Development roadmap
sections.text: Complete reviewed input mappings and current member workflows, expand independent quantity comparisons, resolve native Excel validation and strengthen drawing-to-quantity-to-cost traceability before final release.

sections.title: Lessons from the work
sections.text: Automation is most useful when the origin, unit and assumption behind each quantity remain inspectable. A successful script run and a reconciled spreadsheet are distinct from an approved engineering estimate.
